findings.evidenceJa: 扉越しに気だるそうな声
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s languid voice reaches Shirou through the closed door.
findings.explanation: The English omits the door-mediated location.

findings.evidenceJa: なにやら慌しい気配がする
findings.governingReading: Shirou hears signs of hurried activity after Sakura says she must change.
findings.explanation: The English invents the purpose of meeting him rather than preserving the inferred changing activity.

findings.governingReading: Approximately two minutes pass while Sakura changes.
findings.explanation: The English removes approximation.

findings.governingReading: Sakura says she had been asleep for a little while.
findings.explanation: The English omits the limited duration.

findings.highlight: I don’t know if anything went on
findings.evidenceJa: 物音とか聞いてなくて
findings.governingReading: Because she slept, Sakura did not hear household noises.
findings.explanation: The English changes missing sensory information into general ignorance about events.

findings.evidenceJa: 桜の安眠を邪魔してしまった
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes that his visit has disturbed Sakura’s peaceful sleep.
findings.explanation: The English keeps waking but drops the restful quality he regrets interrupting.

findings.highlight: You should know about your own body
findings.governingReading: Shirou reassures himself that Sakura understands her own body.
findings.explanation: The English turns his trust into a rebuke about what she ought to know.

findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that Sakura would not overexert herself while she has a fever.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the concrete fever.

findings.governingReading: Shirou visibly slumps as he ruefully reflects that he was overprotective.
findings.explanation: The English removes posture, deflation, and self-reproach.

findings.highlight: it makes me feel like I’m sick
findings.evidenceJa: 寝込んでいたら病人みたい
findings.governingReading: Remaining laid up in bed makes Sakura feel like an invalid.
findings.explanation: The English makes resting cause a subjective feeling of sickness rather than resemble being bedridden ill.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺一人では聞いてくれなくて
findings.governingReading: Shirou alone first stops Sakura from doing laundry; Rin intervenes only when Sakura will not heed him.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the initial intervention to a group, blurring Rin’s later entry and Shirou’s failure.

findings.evidenceJa: とんでもなくきつい一言
findings.governingReading: Rin’s threat is one extraordinarily severe line, far beyond gentle assistance.
findings.explanation: The English drops both magnitude and the single decisive utterance.

findings.governingReading: Shirou heads toward the guest-room exit.
findings.explanation: The English omits the spatial movement and temporary-room setting.

findings.governingReading: Sakura catches the hem of Shirou’s shirt to stop him.
findings.explanation: The English drops the small, hesitant point of contact.

findings.governingReading: Sakura rarely depends on Shirou or permits herself to seek affection and indulgence.
findings.explanation: “Demands” makes her unusual vulnerability sound assertive and entitled.

findings.evidenceJa: 精神力を消費していった
findings.governingReading: Being alone with Sakura consumes more of Shirou’s self-control than expected.
findings.explanation: The English turns depletion of restraint into generic nervousness.

findings.highlight: I can see her bare neck
findings.evidenceJa: 少し視線をさげるだけで
findings.governingReading: Only a slight lowering of Shirou’s gaze reveals Sakura’s bare neck and alluring chest.
findings.explanation: The English omits the tiny eye movement structuring his embarrassment.

findings.highlight: if I look at her too closely
findings.evidenceJa: 下手に桜を見てしまうと
findings.governingReading: If Shirou carelessly lets himself look at Sakura, he fears losing control.
findings.explanation: The English changes risky looking at all into scrutiny at close range.

findings.evidenceJa: 隣りには遠坂たちがいる
findings.governingReading: Rin and the others, including Illya, are immediately next door.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the nearby group to Rin alone.

findings.governingReading: Shirou imagines being despised for sexual activity in broad daylight or the middle of the day.
findings.explanation: “Early” changes the social impropriety into clock time.

findings.governingReading: Sakura has become strangely subdued and lacking in energy after being ignored.
findings.explanation: The English promotes an observed loss of spirits into a definite emotional diagnosis.

findings.evidenceJa: 桜にとって今の状況がどんなものなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that he was asking what the present household arrangement feels like for Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English removes Sakura’s focalized experience and makes it a shared situation.

findings.evidenceJa: それと同じぐらい不安
findings.governingReading: Sakura is as anxious about Rin’s presence as she is happy about it.
findings.explanation: The English retains both emotions but deletes their equal weight.

findings.evidenceJa: 未熟なままの自分にとっては眩しすぎて目に痛い
findings.governingReading: For her still-immature self, an embodied ideal is painfully dazzling to look at.
findings.explanation: The English deletes immaturity and the light/vision metaphor, replacing both with generic inferiority.

findings.evidenceJa: ワンパンチされかねない
findings.governingReading: Shirou fears the question could earn him a one-punch response from Rin.
findings.explanation: The English drops the comic one-blow specificity.

findings.governingReading: Sakura admires Rin’s consistently dashing, brisk, heroic bearing.
findings.explanation: “Dignified” changes active stylish vigor into stately decorum.

findings.highlight: I want to be as cool as her
findings.governingReading: Sakura wishes that, even once, she could carry herself as coolly as Rin.
findings.explanation: The English omits the modest once-only limit.

findings.governingReading: Shirou has mixed feelings because Sakura idealizes another girl he admires.
findings.explanation: The English invents reluctance to concede Rin’s merits.

findings.governingReading: Sakura feared that even wanting more from the relationship would make Rin dislike her.
findings.explanation: The English delays the transgression from desire itself to an explicit request.

findings.governingReading: The written Matou name is read as “my,” making inherited family practice overlap Sakura’s personal identity.
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the personal reading and loses the written family layer.

findings.highlight: no set limitation on how you use your magic
findings.evidenceJa: 用途を定められていない
findings.governingReading: Magecraft generally does not begin with one predetermined purpose or end.
findings.explanation: The English turns absence of a fixed purpose into broad freedom in methods of use.

findings.highlight: is to accomplish something and to create a phenomenon
findings.evidenceJa: 何かをなし得るために、何らかの現象を起こす
findings.governingReading: Magecraft causes some phenomenon as a means to accomplish an end.
findings.explanation: The English makes accomplishment and phenomenon two parallel purposes.

findings.highlight: Strengthening is one of the only things I can do
findings.evidenceJa: できる事は決まってる
findings.governingReading: What the operation can produce is fixed or bounded.
findings.explanation: The English changes an operation’s constraints into Shirou having only a few personal abilities.

findings.governingReading: Shirou judges the imposed arts as morally inhumane or outside the proper path.
findings.explanation: The English turns an ethical characterization into religious doctrinal error.

findings.highlight: I’m fine with getting hurt by others
findings.evidenceJa: 人に傷つけられるのは楽
findings.governingReading: Sakura says imposed injury is comparatively easy for her to endure.
findings.explanation: “Fine with” sounds like approval or indifference rather than ease under coercion.

findings.governingReading: Practical demonstrations before Rin differ greatly from his private storehouse training.
findings.explanation: The English drops the magnitude.

findings.governingReading: Sakura’s evaluation feels like receiving the grading of an exam.
findings.explanation: The English changes the awaited judgment into the exam itself.

findings.highlight: does that mean I got a failing score
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether the score is “red,” invoking a failing red mark, and Sakura escalates it to bright red.
findings.explanation: The English communicates failure but removes the color mechanism and Sakura’s matching escalation.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路を発現させる
findings.governingReading: Shirou experiences manifesting or bringing his existing magical circuit into operation as an act near death.
findings.explanation: The English says he creates a circuit, changing the ontology.

findings.evidenceJa: 内部に張り巡らした集中
findings.governingReading: His concentration is stretched or laid throughout his interior like a network.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the spatially distributed internal construction.

findings.governingReading: Shirou believes this is an ordinary price paid for magecraft.
findings.explanation: “Compensation” reverses a cost into something received in recompense.

findings.governingReading: Shirou supposes his genuinely hazardous practice results only from inexperience.
findings.explanation: The English turns danger into outward appearance.

findings.highlight: creates a new Magic Circuit for each spell
findings.evidenceJa: 毎回その為だけに魔術回路を発現させる
findings.governingReading: Shirou abnormally manifests his magical circuit afresh each time solely to perform magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English says a new circuit is created for every spell, materially changing the mechanism.

findings.highlight: Every night, you did something that could kill you
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を殺す事を毎晩やっていました
findings.governingReading: Sakura characterizes his nightly practice as repeatedly killing himself.
findings.explanation: The English weakens deliberate repeated self-destruction into exposure to possible death.

findings.highlight: you didn’t get anything out of it
findings.governingReading: He persisted without coercion and not even for his own sake.
findings.explanation: The English changes motive into absence of personal payoff.

findings.governingReading: He upheld the practice alone for the entire period.
findings.explanation: The English omits the sustained solitude.

findings.governingReading: Shirou objects using circuits and magical characteristics as practical measures of strength.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a technical magical characteristic with general talent.

findings.governingReading: Sakura’s happy gaze revives the impure, obsessive desire Shirou had suppressed.
findings.explanation: The English reduces morally and erotically charged fixation to distraction.

findings.governingReading: Shirou explicitly agrees to wait before asking what Sakura wants.
findings.explanation: The English omits the immediate reassurance.

findings.highlight: I’m sure it’ll move fine by tomorrow
findings.evidenceJa: 明日には普通に動くんじゃないかな
findings.governingReading: Shirou tentatively predicts ordinary movement by tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The English changes a hopeful forecast into confidence.

findings.governingReading: The written Matou name is again read as “my,” binding inherited family art to Sakura’s self-conception.
findings.explanation: The English preserves only the spoken self-reference and loses the family layer.

findings.evidenceJa: ウトウトと舟をこぎながら
findings.governingReading: Sakura actually nods and bobs as she dozes while speaking.
findings.explanation: The English reduces physical near-sleep to appearance.

findings.governingReading: Shirou quietly leaves the guest room after turning off the light.
findings.explanation: The English again converts temporary guest accommodation into Sakura’s own room.

findings.highlight: I saw Sakura fall asleep peacefully
findings.evidenceJa: 穏やかな桜の寝顔を見た
findings.governingReading: Shirou has looked at Sakura’s peaceful sleeping face.
findings.explanation: The English changes a lingering visual image into witnessing the event of falling asleep.

findings.highlight: be on your guard against me
findings.evidenceJa: わたしを見張っていて
findings.governingReading: The isolated phrase asks Shirou to keep watch over or monitor Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English explicitly casts Sakura as a threat he must guard against.
